public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
CruxOCM is a Series A climate and energy company co-founded by Roger Shirt and Vicki Knott that has raised $26.1M to date. The valuation exercise draws on a comp universe of 9 private frontier-tech peers in Climate & Energy (including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix) and 1 public comparable (LNZA).

A stage-progression methodology is applicable here. Using the $26.1M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $52.2M. A peer-median approach could not be reliably deployed due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow Climate & Energy peer set; the 8 same-sector peers lack the density needed (≥3 datapoints) for meaningful triangulation without introducing downstream sector-level noise.

The triangulated valuation range is $44M–$60M, centered at $52M. This single-method result carries material uncertainty: the lack of tight peer comparables limits validation of the stage-progression output, and the frontier nature of climate-tech businesses means public market multiples offer limited guidance. Key sensitivities include capital efficiency relative to peers and stage-specific dilution assumptions embedded in the 2.0x multiplier. Additional data on peer financing rounds and unit economics would refine this range materially.
